segments.title: Three Victorian naval diplomacy crises
segments.summary: The opening introduces the crises at Constantinople, Alexandria, and Tangier, three major cases of Victorian naval diplomacy between 1878 and 1906.
segments.body: Constantinople, Alexandria, and Tangier form the three cases for the longer discussion, covering 1878 to 1906. The period is only 28 years, yet it includes three major incidents. Together they form a compact comparison of Victorian naval diplomacy in the Mediterranean. Start here for the places, dates, and scope of the argument.

evidence.note: The presenter introduces naval diplomacy through Constantinople, Alexandria, and Tangier, dating the cases to 1878–1906.

segments.title: When naval pressure succeeds - or escalates
segments.summary: Two crises suffered from muddled diplomatic and naval handling. A naval officer's quick action partly rescued one, while local naval realities made another worse.
segments.body: One crisis became violent, while the other two stopped short of armed conflict. Two cases suffered from muddled diplomacy and poor naval handling. A naval officer's quick action partly rescued one of those cases by forcing the issue. In the other, local naval conditions made the crisis worse.

evidence.note: The presenter contrasts a conflict that became hot, muddled handling, decisive local action, and naval conditions that exacerbated a crisis.

segments.title: Coordinated policy backed by Gibraltar
segments.summary: The final crisis achieved the best result with the least impact because diplomatic and naval plans worked together under clear guidance, with Gibraltar in the background.
segments.body: The final crisis had clear guidance and a common purpose for diplomatic and naval plans. Their coordination produced the best result with the least impact. It is the clearest case in the comparison of naval force supporting policy instead of complicating it. Gibraltar's presence in the background also favored the operation, so coordination was only part of the advantage.

evidence.note: The presenter credits strong guidance and common purpose between naval and diplomatic plans for the least damaging outcome, while noting Gibraltar's supporting presence.
